provenance.l: Apollo 16 Mission Report MSC-07230 (Aug 1972): Table 3-III, entry interface 265:37:31 at 400,000 ft, 36,196.1 ft/s (11,033 m/s), flight-path angle -6.55 deg (OCR of the scan); Table A-IV, command module weight at entry 13,015 lb (5,904 kg; OCR, the CM after separation reads 13,026); Table 3-I drogues 265:45:26 (the pilot noted large oscillations on the drogues), mains 265:46:16, all three mains good; landing at 265:51:05 GET (19:45:05 GMT 27 April 1972) at 0 deg 42.0 min S, 156 deg 12.8 min W (computer), 3 n.mi from the target, USS Ticonderoga. Quote: "Landing occurred at 1945 G.m.t." The command module landed flat and hard (Stable I, then Stable II, uprighted in about 4.5 min); the model has no water-impact load

NASA SP-4029 Apollo chronology, "Entry, Splashdown, and Recovery" compilation (Apollo 7-17): Apollo 16 column: "Lift To Drag Ratio 0.286", "Range (n mi) 1,190" (1,190 n.mi = 2,204 km), "Maximum g 7.19" (the Flight Journal PAD predicted 6.87), "Duration (sec) 814.0", velocity 36,196.1 ft/s, flight-path angle -6.55, splashdown 0.70 S 156.22 W, landing weight 11,995 lb. No Entry Postflight Analysis exists for Apollo 16 (the mission report's supplement list has none), so L/D and range are the compilation values (secondary), not a reconstruction; no first/second load-factor split is published. Model limit (US Standard Atmosphere 1976, 2026-11-25): with these inputs the model's first pulse is 6.8 g at 81 s (7.19 g flown), it dips to 1.9 g, second pulse 6.7 g; drogues 421 s (475 s flown, 265:45:26), splashdown 769 s (814 s flown). The larger pulse is within 10% of the flown maximum g; the entry runs short of the flown time, a limit of the fixed-bank planar guidance (on Apollo 11, the one flight with a published minimum, it lofts to 0.8 g between the pulses against the flown 0.48 g). Flotation (B1): NASA SP-4029, "Entry, Splashdown, and Recovery" table, Apollo 16 column: flotation attitude "Inverted" (stable II), uprighting time "4.5" minutes (realAfterS 270 s). When the capsule turned over is not given: drawn 3 s after splashdown
Apollo CM entry aero (L/D 0.3), drogue and main areas: the Apollo 8 profile (MSC-PA-R-69-1), same Block II command module
